name: VidVerge
description: VidVerge brings two focused video workflows together: create polished product videos or enhance footage you already have.

agent.name: VidVerge Director
agent.welcomeMessage: Welcome to VidVerge. Bring me a product URL, a script, rough footage, or simply the outcome you want — I’ll help turn the brief into a polished, publish-ready video.

apps.name: Video Enhancer
apps.description: Professional timeline editor (NLE) for footage you already have — a three-panel dark editor: a 16:9 preview player with play/pause, timecode, volume and fullscreen; an AI Tools + Properties band; and a four-track timeline (Video / Graphics / Audio / Captions) with clips as colored blocks, drag-to-reorder, split-at-playhead and per-clip delete, trim handles on every clip edge, an amber playhead synced to the player and click-to-seek, plus a 16:9 / 9:16 TikTok format toggle that carries through to the export. The headline tool is one-click AI EDIT: it transcribes the footage's own audio with word timestamps, cuts the dead air automatically (Web Audio silence detection becomes real timeline cuts), lays word-accurate amber captions, and places AI-planned kinetic motion graphics on the Graphics track. Individually: Gemini Describe analyzes a video frame (subject, dominant-color swatches, mood badge, suggested enhancements as amber pills) and fires automatically on upload; Generate B-roll turns a prompt into an Omni Flash clip on the Video track; Auto-transcribe makes word-timed captions on its own (manual transcript paste stays as a fallback); Style Transfer applies Cinematic / Vibrant / Dark / Vintage / Minimal looks; and five quality-first Quick Motion Graphics presets — Hook Title (word-by-word kinetic headline with an underline sweep), Keyword Pop (overshoot pop with an amber glow), Lower Third (name + handle on a growing accent bar), Big Stat (count-up number in a glowing ring) and CTA Banner (rising pill with a pulsing glow) — drop at the playhead, drag to retime, and are fully editable (text, sub line, value, duration, position). The preview and the server render share the same easing math, so what you see is what renders. Properties edit the selected clip (in/out trim, split at playhead, delete, 0.5×–2× speed, opacity, a text overlay) or the selected graphic, plus whole-video Effects (brightness / contrast / saturation / blur / vignette sliders, previewed live and applied identically in the render), the music bed (Inspiring / Cinematic Dark / Energetic / Calm / Luxury from the workspace's ElevenLabs library, or GENERATE YOUR OWN: describe a track and ElevenLabs composes it to the cut's length) and the color grade (None / Film / Kodak / Teal+Orange / BW). Upload by drag-and-drop or file picker (up to 500MB). Render & Export compiles the whole edit — cuts, trims, speed, opacity, text, motion graphics, captions, effects, grade, format and music — into a server-side Remotion render and hands back a downloadable 1080p MP4 (9:16 renders the centered TikTok stage). Also the handoff target for SceneForge: a finished SceneForge video opened "in the Editor" or "sent to the Enhancer" loads here automatically as the first clip.

apps.name: Script-to-Video
apps.description: The rebuilt script-to-film pipeline with Claude Opus 5 as the single director brain: paste a script (never rewritten) and Opus breaks it into independent scenes, deciding per scene how it gets made — cinematic live-action shots on Veo (with a hard rule against on-screen text), deterministic motion graphics rendered in the browser with HTML/SVG + GSAP (eleven varied treatments — kinetic type, documentary lower-thirds, flowcharts, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, timelines, comparisons, node maps, quotes, annotated images — each with its own content-matched palette, never a repeated generic card), real product screenshots inside animated phone/laptop/browser mockups (Veo is never asked to recreate a UI), and reused project assets with cinematic motion and exact labels. Continuity is frame-chained: after each Veo scene the last frame is extracted and Opus reads its visual attributes (lighting, character, environment, camera) into the next scene's prompt, so consecutive cinematic shots carry the same person, place and light; independent scenes render in parallel. After every render Opus checks the clip against its script segment and flags mismatches. Every scene is independent — own spec, status, cached clip — so regenerating one scene never touches the rest, and a docked Director bar revises any single scene from a plain-English note. Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser: normalization, audio handling and the final MP4 cut, no server renderer. On the Final screen, an opt-in Finish step can add ElevenLabs narration from the untouched original script, an ElevenLabs music bed automatically ducked beneath narration and native scene sound, and scene-timed burned-in captions built from each stored script segment and measured duration; generated tracks and settings are persisted and reused. Runs persist to the database at every step and resume after reloads. Legacy projects stay watchable in the Library.

apps.name: SceneForge
apps.description: SceneForge v4 is a talking-head + documentary motion-graphics studio: the HeyGen avatar master carries the film (intro, transitions and CTA on camera) while MIDDLE VISUAL SECTIONS cut in over its picture and the presenter's narration keeps playing underneath, documentary style. The single orchestrator LLM writes the script, then produces a full video blueprint: every middle scene gets a customer-switchable type — AI VIDEO (real generated footage on Gemini Omni Flash; an unchanged prompt reuses its clip), MOTION GRAPHIC (the new GSAP + SVG engine: branching diagrams, flowcharts, timelines, comparisons, list reveals, big-stat count-ups, bar charts, node graphs, annotated images and text reveals, all rendered from a structured spec whose every string and number appears EXACTLY as written — important text never goes inside AI video; scenes preview live in the browser and are captured with MediaRecorder into real video clips), IMAGE (one strong Omni Flash still), or TEXT OVERLAY (a deterministic animated headline captured the same way). The blueprint timeline is colour-coded: HeyGen blue, AI video purple, motion graphics green, images orange, text teal. Scenes are independently editable — switching a type or editing a spec regenerates ONLY that scene, every clip is cached, re-assembly never re-renders finished scenes, and the HeyGen master stays locked unless explicitly re-recorded. Final assembly composites the middle clips over the continuous avatar master: 9:16 films run through the platform's server-side FFmpeg overlay compositor (base narration audio kept uninterrupted), 16:9 films use one deterministic compositing render because the platform's FFmpeg compositor is portrait-only today. Steps: topic → deep-research script → live HeyGen v3 avatar render (resumable after reload) → style → blueprint review with live GSAP previews and per-scene capture → parallel middle-visual production with per-scene Retry / switch type / Skip → audio-preserving assembly, six quality checks, inline player, ElevenLabs music bed under a 16:9 master → editor handoff — plus the built-in Asset Studio (Omni Flash stills attached straight onto scenes, always reused, never re-billed) and natural-language script/scene/style/assembly changes via Verger.

apps.name: Ads Studio
apps.description: Agentic short-form ad engine: product URL + avatar + assets in, a finished professional ad out. A linear 8-step workflow (Product → Research → Angles → Script → Scene Plan → Generate → Review → Variations) with Claude Opus 5 as the single creative brain. Research crawls the product site (plus /reviews, /testimonials, /pricing and /about) and extracts a structured direct-response brief — features, pricing, pain points, desires, objections, mechanism, awareness level and real customer language, each marked [VERIFIED] or [INFERRED], never invented — that the user can correct inline. Opus then generates 8–12 genuinely different ad angles (selectable cards with an 'Opus picks best' judge), writes a 4–7 clip script (Hook → Problem → Agitate → Solution → Proof → Benefit → single CTA) under hard per-duration word limits (4s→9, 6s→13, 8s→17, 10s→22 words) with live word-count validation and per-clip duration selectors, and directs a full per-clip scene plan — camera, framing, micro-action, gesture, expression, environment, lighting, ONE locked voice description reused verbatim across all clips, continuity notes, overlay plan and an assembled production Veo prompt (clip 1 must open on a first-second pattern interrupt, never a static talking head). Generation is an agentic loop: each clip renders on the platform video model with the uploaded avatar as the character reference, Opus vision inspects the take against the plan (action, framing, flow, same character, clutter, composition), a rejected take auto-regenerates ONCE with the inspector's adjusted prompt (max 2 attempts), and the final frame of each clip is read by Opus into the next clip's continuity clause. Real screenshots are never recreated by the video model — they composite AFTER generation inside GSAP-animated phone/laptop/browser/tablet/monitor mockups, alongside kinetic text callouts, review cards, animated stat counters, CTA buttons, arrow highlights, a logo watermark and styled burned-in captions of each spoken line (all GSAP + SVG rendered to canvas, no Remotion). Final assembly runs FFmpeg.wasm in the browser — chroma-keyed overlay compositing, normalization, concat, faststart MP4 — with a progress bar, a collapsible FFmpeg debug log and a download button. A Variations step has Opus write alternative hooks, bodies and CTAs (up to 3×2×2 = 12 combinations); building a variation reuses every clip whose line is unchanged and regenerates only the clips whose spoken line differs, then re-assembles, each with its own download. The session persists to localStorage, so a refresh resumes mid-run. A RECIPES section in the left rail (below the eight steps) holds the Runway-powered recipe templates — Product Ads, UGC, Product Swaps, Multi-Shot films, Localized Ads, Campaign Imagery and Stock Images — plus raw text/image-to-video on the Runway Gen 4 models (Gen 4.5 and Gen 4 Turbo); every generation is quoted before anything is charged, and this is now the ONE place Runway recipes live (the standalone Runway tabs in Product Video, SceneForge and Script-to-Video were removed). Standalone — shares nothing with Product Video, SceneForge, Video Enhancer or Script-to-Video.

apps.name: MotionVerger
apps.description: The dedicated SaaS LAUNCH VIDEO studio — one job, zero configuration: paste a product URL and get a 15–45 second kinetic product-demo film that is cut differently on every single run. The app reads the real page server-side via the ps-brand-scrape hook (product name, tagline, headlines, feature bullets, the site's exact CTA wording, logo, a live screenshot, and the brand colours the markup actually uses), then gpt-5.6-terra writes a LIBRARY of candidate lines out of that real copy (hooks, features, use cases, outcomes and any genuine social proof) and the app's own composition engine cuts it into a film. There is no scene blueprint any more: the arc, the scene count, their order, each shot's length (2–5s), the camera move, the transition and the colour grade are all rolled from a per-generation seed, so the same URL never renders the same film twice — a 'Shuffle the cut' button re-rolls the edit from the same page with no re-scrape, and every cut lands inside 15–45s. If the writer hiccups the page's own mined copy still composes a complete film, so a run never dead-ends. The customer can edit every headline, supporting line and duration, pick a music bed from the shared cached ElevenLabs library (or turn music off), then Generate renders a deterministic Remotion composition server-side via the pv-render-composition hook (1920x1080, 30fps MP4): a living brand-tinted gradient background with drifting glow blobs and a subtle grid, word-by-word spring kinetic typography, feature cards with growing accent bars, the customer's REAL screenshot inside a drawn browser frame being USED — a cursor travels to a control, clicks, the work runs on a progress bar and a result chip lands — under a pulling-BACK camera (every move in the film is a zoom-out or a pan; nothing ever zooms in) and a light sweep (a brand-coloured interface skeleton when the page gave none), and a pulsing CTA plate carrying the site's exact call-to-action and host — all in the CLIENT's own colour and logo, never VidVerge amber. NO narration, NO image model, NO invented UI: every visual is drawn in code, so nothing that is not theirs can appear in the film. Projects persist to the mv_projects table; an in-flight render survives tab close and reload and resumes polling on reopen; finished films live in a 'Your launch videos' gallery with a Download MP4 button and one-click re-render. Distinct from Product Video: MotionVerger is the fast single-purpose launch-film path, while Product Video remains the deeper multi-workflow studio.

apps.name: Character Generator
apps.description: Design reusable video characters for the whole VidVerge suite. Describe a character (name, appearance, personality, style tags) and optionally upload a reference photo — VidVerge reads the photo with AI vision and pre-writes the appearance. Generate renders a consistent character card with an AI portrait (platform image pipeline, 3:4, portrait-safe negative prompts), previewed live as a card with the name and style tags. Saving writes the character to the shared vv_characters WorkspaceDB table (name, description, style, image_url, reference_images) so SceneForge, Script-to-Video and Ads Studio can reuse the exact same person across every scene. Previously generated characters appear in a grid below with Reuse (loads the character back into the form to tweak and regenerate) and Delete. LightBeam dark UI, amber accent, session-scoped rows.
